chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Los Angeles: record crowds and Ella's film
summary: The band broke attendance records out west while Ella made a Hollywood picture; four big bands were in town.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We played in Los Angeles. Ella did a -- I think she did Ride 'Em Cowboy. Abbott and Costello, that picture, she did that
Yeah. She did that picture and --
We were playing at the ballroom there -- a famous ballroom out there in California where all the bands play, Duke played (inaudible).
There was a Cotton Club out there.
No, we didn't play no clubs. We played just ballrooms like the Savoy here (inaudible).

I'll tell you afterwhile. Anyway, when we opened out there, we broke everybody's record. We broke Duke's record, Jimmie Lunceford's record, Basie's record. We had more people than any band who ever walked in that place.

And the man that came -- when Ella was making a picture -- he came out to catch the band. He says, "Why didn't Moe Gale tell him about how great this band was," you know. People in moving pictures don't know. They're in one part of the world and we're in our part of the world, and somebody's in their part of the world. What goes in Hollywood, you asked them about something, "You know so and so?" "No, I don't know." See, they live in a different atmosphere altogether. When he heard the band -- Ella say, "Come out and catch the band." He did come out. And he heard the band -- he say, "Why didn't Moe Gale tell me this band was this good? We could've used the band in the picture." We're sitting out there doing nothing, waiting until Ella finish doing the picture for a week, you know. But then after we went downtown -- we

played a theater downtown like the Paramount here, you know. And that's where we had -- we had to bring people, (inaudible) like the Paramount had cops on horses all out in front of the theater, holding the crowd back and everything.
And I think Fats Waller was there. He was playing another theater.
I think at that time, there was four bands in town. Fats Waller was in town with his band, because my brother, Dave, was playing with Fats at that time.
And Jimmy Lunceford -- I think Jimmy was in town. No, Jimmy wasn't in town. Basie was in town, Duke was in town.
I know there was four big bands in town.
All these bands was in town and every one of them was doing something.
